svg.title: Pushing versus pulling a block of ice
svg.desc: As the angle of the applied force grows, pushing down at the angle increases the normal force, while pulling up at the angle reduces it, so pulling always needs less force to start the block. At 25 degrees the starting forces are 51.0 and 46.5 newtons. Animated motion has a static alternative for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Pulling at an angle beats pushing
Push: N = mg + F sin θ
Pull: N = mg − F sin θ
45.0-kg ice block, μₛ = 0.10. The force angle sweeps from 0° to 40°; dots mark the exercise’s 25°
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
